content: Deglycyrrhizinated licorice, commonly referred to as DGL, is an herbal supplement frequently used in the treatment of gastric and duodenal ulcers. It is derived from licorice root, with the glycyrrhizin component removed to reduce potential side effects associated with glycyrrhizin. The standard recommended dosage of DGL is 760 mg, which is typically chewed approximately 20 minutes before a meal. Clinical studies conducted on both humans and animals have demonstrated that DGL significantly reduces the size of gastric ulcers and accelerates the healing process. In one study, 44% of participants experienced complete healing of their ulcers, compared to only 6% in the placebo group. DGL has also been shown to be an effective treatment for duodenal ulcers. In a study where participants consumed 5 grams of DGL daily for 12 weeks, all subjects exhibited substantial improvement, with higher dosages yielding the most pronounced therapeutic effects. Furthermore, additional research has indicated that the efficacy of DGL in treating ulcers is comparable to that of cimetidine, a commonly used H2 receptor antagonist. There have been no documented cases of DGL overdose, and reported side effects are minimal, with occasional instances of nausea and diarrhea. Additionally, no known drug interactions have been identified between DGL and medications commonly used to treat ulcers. In regions such as Europe, South Africa, and Canada, DGL is marketed as a medicinal preparation under the name Caved-S. In other areas, it is available as an herbal supplement. Beyond its use for gastric and duodenal ulcers, DGL has also been reported to aid in the treatment of aphthous ulcers, commonly known as canker sores.
